clinician.final_diagnosis: COPD bullous emphysema with superimposed pneumonia
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 42-year-old woman from Sierra Leone with no smoking history or typical COPD risk factors presented with 1 week of progressive productive cough, dyspnea, fatigue, and palpitations. On examination, she had bilateral rales and rhonchi with exertional desaturation (69% on room air after ambulation). Chest CT revealed bilateral emphysematous changes with multiple prominent pulmonary bullae (largest in anterior left upper lobe and posterior right lower lobes), bronchiectasis, bronchial wall thickening, and pulmonary vascular dilatation. Alpha-1 antitrypsin was normal, ruling out hereditary predisposition. Respiratory culture grew Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Candida albicans, confirming superimposed pneumonia. She was treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics (vancomycin, cefepime, doxycycline), supplemental oxygen, methylprednisolone, and bronchodilators (albuterol/ipratropium). At 2-week follow-up, symptoms improved significantly. Spirometry demonstrated severe COPD with FEV1 of 23% and FEV1/FVC ratio of 65%. She was discharged on maintenance therapy with Trelegy Ellipta and albuterol as needed.
